analysis.title: Left behind by the squeeze
key_insights: Yesterday's monster squeeze in AI names did not fix deeper problems. Several former AI darlings are back under heavy selling and valuation compression across parts of the AI value chain is extreme.

Bernstein's analysis of 66 stocks across nine sectors finds data center exposure explains roughly 45% of the variation in valuation compression. Memory and server OEMs saw the largest dislocations while networking held up better.

SNDK traded at 2.5x forward earnings at Friday's close versus a three-year average of 10.4x. The 76% multiple compression is almost twice what Bernstein's data center exposure model implies, so the market doubts earnings sustainability.

SNDK is technically deeply oversold, has been oversold since October and has more than halved since. It trades well below its 200-day MA with the 50-day about to cross below it. The note flags a possible contrarian trade but warns oversold can persist.

Memory blind spot: SNDK's new customer agreements cover about 50% of FY27 bit volumes and two-thirds of FY28 volumes with volume commitments, pricing mechanisms and financial protections. Bernstein estimates HBF at 5% of NAND bit demand would require about 28% more wafers.
Storage over memory: STX and WDC traded at 9.2x and 8.3x forward earnings at Friday's close. Bernstein sees the HDD pricing upcycle as early stage and prefers STX for its HAMR technology lead.

CRWV still screens as under-punished in Bernstein's analysis despite the reset. The issue is converting contracted demand into profitable capacity after depreciation and financing costs. The stock is at must-hold levels with credit spreads exploding.
NBIS remains under intense selling despite the squeeze, a worrying sign. $80 is major support but there is a large unfilled gap below.

AVGO is Bernstein's top US semiconductor pick at roughly 15x 2027 and 9x 2028 estimated earnings. Customers are among the best capitalized and the stock sits at major support and the long-term trendline, far below its 200-day MA.
CIEN could benefit from power and land constraints because smaller dispersed data centers need scale-across networking. Bernstein highlights CIEN as particularly exposed.
